CH.coreZoneText: Danger level "considerable" (3=) in west to north to east facing aspects above 2800m.

avalancheProblems.comment:
Over a wide area 50 to 70 cm of snow will fall on Wednesday above approximately 2800 m. The new snow will be deposited on the unfavourable surface of an old snowpack in particular on steep shady slopes in high Alpine regions. Persons can release avalanches, including large ones. Natural avalanches are possible.
The current avalanche situation calls for experience in the assessment of avalanche danger.
The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field, so that the avalanche danger should be investigated especially thoroughly in the relevant locality.

snowpackStructure.comment:
Snowpack

Over the past two weeks, some snow fell in the high mountains, with the largest amounts along the main Alpine ridge from the Monte Rosa region to the Bernina region. This snow has partly undergone faceting. Further snowfall is expected on Wednesday. On shady slopes in the high mountains, the fresh snow will fall on a partly continuous old snowpack. In these areas, fractures may occur at the interface between the old and fresh snow, particularly on glaciers. Elsewhere, the snow will generally fall on bare ground. In these areas, weak layers are most likely to occur within the fresh snow and wind slabs.

tendency.comment:
Outlook

Thursday

During the night to Thursday, some precipitation will persist in the north. During the day, it will be mostly sunny, but remain cloudy in the east. The wind will be moderate to strong from the northwest.

The danger of dry avalanches will gradually decrease. Wet loose snow avalanches are to be expected on steep sun-exposed slopes in the high mountains.

Friday

On Friday, it will be variably cloudy with occasional precipitation, especially in the west. In the east, it will remain dry with sunny intervals. The snowfall level will be around 1500 m. The southwesterly wind will strengthen, reaching storm force, with a southerly foehn in the Alpine valleys.

The southwesterly wind may give rise to wind slabs that are prone to triggering. In the high mountains, people can still trigger avalanches, particularly on steep north-facing slopes.

CH.coreZoneText: Danger level "moderate" (2=) in west to north to east facing aspects above 2800m.

avalancheProblems.comment:
Over a wide area 20 to 40 cm of snow will fall on Wednesday above approximately 2800 m. As a consequence of a moderate southwesterly wind, sometimes avalanche prone wind slabs will form in particular adjacent to ridgelines and in gullies and bowls as well as at elevated altitudes. These can in some places be released by people. Avalanches can reach medium size.
Backcountry touring calls for careful route selection.
The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field, so that the avalanche danger should be investigated especially thoroughly in the relevant locality.
